evidence.title: README.md
evidence.locator: Features; Getting Started; OpenCode V2; Requirements
evidence.finding: Electron and Tauri desktop clients on three OSes and standalone npm server. OpenCode shared service owns execution and sessions. Git worktrees, remote access, browser previews, MCP and plugin controls are described.

evidence.title: docs/help/en/missions.md
evidence.locator: Create then explicitly start; Follow the tree; Launch criteria; Controls and recovery
evidence.finding: Durable paused missions have coordinator/delegates, dependency task trees, reports, explicit start, schedules/events and separate pause, interrupt and terminal stop controls. Native schedules require experimental.schedules and supported OpenCode.

evidence.title: docs/help/en/providers.md
evidence.locator: Connect; Select and manage accounts; Automatic selection limits; Usage
evidence.finding: Native OpenCode OAuth/API-key connections and service-wide saved accounts are supported. Codex subscription OAuth and OpenCode Claude Pro/Max OAuth are distinguished from Claude Code login. Usage quotas and cost estimates are not bills.

evidence.title: docs/help/en/mobile.md
evidence.locator: Connect; PWA; Capability and connectivity limits
evidence.finding: Phone/tablet browser and PWA can operate the reachable backend. No offline backend; closing PWA leaves standalone backend running, while quitting host desktop backend disables Remote Control.

evidence.title: docs/help/en/permissions.md
evidence.locator: Permission requests and session controls
evidence.finding: Permission dock exposes native OpenCode requests; actions retain native scope. UI distinguishes permission responses from already-running shell/tool cancellation.

evidence.title: PRIVACY.md
evidence.locator: Privacy policy; Automatic connections
evidence.finding: CodeNomad says it has no product accounts, telemetry, analytics or advertising. Local projects/conversations/settings remain on host; OpenCode sends content to configured providers. Release/UI update and package requests remain.

evidence.title: LICENSE
evidence.locator: MIT License
evidence.finding: Application source is MIT licensed.

evidence.title: v1.0.1-dev-20261108-175b1820
evidence.locator: Release date and release notes
evidence.finding: v1.0.1-dev-20261108-175b1820 was published 2026-11-08. Release notes describe the scoped changes; this is not a hands-on check.

evidence.title: CodeNomad README
evidence.locator: Getting started ('connect your model provider'); footer licence line
evidence.finding: The user connects their own model provider; the README states no price and marks the project MIT-licensed.

evidence.title: CodeNomad LICENSE
evidence.locator: MIT License, permission grant
evidence.finding: The MIT license grants permission to use, copy, modify and distribute the software free of charge.

evidence.title: CodeNomad help site
evidence.locator: Landing page
evidence.finding: The help site lists language versions only and contains no pricing.

evidence.title: Download CodeNomad
evidence.locator: Page header and Desktop apps section (version 1.0.1)
evidence.finding: The download page describes CodeNomad as a free and open-source (MIT) desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux and offers installers for version 1.0.1; it shows no price or paid plan.

evidence.title: CodeNomad README, installation
evidence.locator: README.md lines 38-70 (desktop and standalone server installation) and line 245 (MIT licence footer), release v1.0.1 commit 3e9cbb1
evidence.finding: Desktop builds download from the releases page and the standalone server runs on the user's host; the README names no price, account or paid plan and marks the project MIT licensed.

evidence.title: CodeNomad Antigravity support at v1.0.1
evidence.locator: packages/server/src/usage/service.test.ts lines 40-55, v1.0.1, commit 3e9cbb122ec1ea41227f278006747cf6222d8aa1
evidence.finding: CodeNomad v1.0.1 is an OpenCode workspace. Its Antigravity references exercise provider usage handling, not a separate Antigravity CLI launch.

evidence.title: CodeNomad Antigravity support at v1.0.1
evidence.locator: README.md lines 1-15, v1.0.1, commit 3e9cbb122ec1ea41227f278006747cf6222d8aa1
evidence.finding: CodeNomad v1.0.1 is an OpenCode workspace. Its Antigravity references exercise provider usage handling, not a separate Antigravity CLI launch.

evidence.title: CodeNomad v1.0.1 source
evidence.locator: OpenCode V2 compatibility and runtime setup; README application install and requirements
evidence.finding: CodeNomad is a workspace around the OpenCode V2 shared runtime. The built-in process/service and compatibility paths target OpenCode, not a generic coding CLI. Its install distribution contains desktop macOS/Windows/Linux and a standalone browser/PWA server, not native iOS/Android apps.

evidence.title: CodeNomad Remote Control
evidence.locator: Manage paired devices; Available and unavailable surfaces
evidence.finding: Up to 32 paired devices can use ordinary conversation APIs, send prompts, inspect files and answer permissions. Pairing grants writable access rather than a read-only sharing link; credentials are per device and revocable.

evidence.title: CodeNomad v1.0.1 source
evidence.locator: Shared workspace/session prompt route; server/remote-proxy.ts activated-device prompt proxy; auth/manager.ts
evidence.finding: Authenticated browser sessions and activated paired-device proxies post to the same workspace/session prompt API. The backend uses a common configured host username; it does not allocate separate agent work by human account. Different authorized clients can send prompts to the shared session.

evidence.title: CodeNomad v1.0.1 source
evidence.locator: AuthManager configured username; auth-store; session-manager; docs/help/en/security.md
evidence.finding: The backend authenticates a configured host username/password or per-device Remote Control credentials. The pinned auth/session and server route paths have no human organization role model or SAML/OIDC SSO integration. Device revocation is separate from password changes.

evidence.title: CodeNomad v1.0.1 source
evidence.locator: Runtime launch/compatibility paths; docs/help/en/security.md Host boundary
evidence.finding: The runtime connects to OpenCode on the user host. Workspace-root restrictions are explicitly not containers or an OS sandbox; native tools act with host permissions. No CodeNomad-managed container/VM task provisioner appears in the inspected server/workspace/runtime implementation.

evidence.title: CodeNomad v1.0.1 source
evidence.locator: ForgeWorkItems service; forge/providers.ts; server/routes/panel-extension-work-items.ts
evidence.finding: The forge integration is explicitly a bounded read-only issue/PR listing API. Bounded source inspection of forge/server Git routes found no native PR create/update/merge operation; Git/worktree controls are separate.

evidence.title: CodeNomad providers and accounts
evidence.locator: Connect a model provider
evidence.finding: Settings > Providers supports native API-key, OAuth or command authentication. Keys are stored by the connected OpenCode server and inference is billed under the connected provider account.
